segmenti.tekst: نَحْنُ نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ أَحْسَنَ الْقَصَصِ بِمَا أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْكَ هَٰذَا الْقُرْآنَ وَإِنْ كُنْتَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ لَمِنَ الْغَافِلِينَ
segmenti.prevod: “We relate to you the best of stories in revealing to you this Qur’an, though before it you were among the unaware.” (Yusuf 12:3)

segmenti.tekst: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى نَبِيِّنَا مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِهِ وَصَحْبِهِ أَجْمَعِينَ
segmenti.prevod: Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad and upon his family and all his companions.

segmenti.tekst: After Yusuf's brothers took Yusuf, alayhis-salatu was-salam (peace be upon him), far away from

the inhabited place, to where they tended their livestock, they agreed among themselves and threw him to the bottom of the well. After that they come to their father, as the Qur'an says: "And they came to their father in the evening, weeping."

Why did they come in the evening? You know, dear brothers, that it is the custom (adet) of those who live in the countryside to go out with their livestock in the morning, stay out all day, and return in the evening.
It is customary: they take something with them, food, drink, and then they return in the evening. Yusuf's brothers did the same. So they came to their father weeping.
That is, it was not real weeping, it was play-acting. And they said to him: "Father," they say, "our father, we were playing, we were racing and so on, and we left Yusuf to look after our things."
Imagine, they left Yusuf, a little boy of seven, to look after their things. And what happened to him? They say: "A wolf ate him.

And," they say, "you will not believe us, even though," they say, "we are telling the truth. Even though we are telling the truth, you will not believe us." Why? Because you love Yusuf very much and you will surely accuse us of some misdeed.
That is: "Our father, what you foresaw has happened to Yusuf." You know, we mentioned it, when Yaqub, alayhis-salatu was-salam, said: "I fear that a wolf may eat him", and they made use of that.

As if he had unintentionally given them the idea of what to do with Yusuf, alayhis-salatu was-salam. How they would, that is, how they tried to justify, to stage it all – they had planned it all out nicely, but there is no, dear brothers, perfect crime.
There is no perfect crime. There is always something the criminal forgets. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: and they came, He says, with his shirt, which they had smeared with blood.

It was smeared with the blood of some animal. Either they slaughtered a sheep, or they killed some other animal, but it was not Yusuf's blood. They took the shirt off Yusuf, smeared it with blood and then brought it to their father.
When the father, Yaqub, saw that the shirt was not torn at all – because, if a wolf had eaten him, then logically the shirt would be torn, but the shirt was whole –

what they thought would be proof in their favour was proof against them. They had not planned everything so well. They had not thought it through well. And Yaqub saw at once that something was not right there.

But the matter was already done. He only said to them: "Sawwalat…" – he says: "Shaytan has made this," he says, "seem fair to you. Your soul, your nafs, that evil one, has made this deed you have done seem fair to you."

What could he do? What is the solution? It says: he endured with beautiful patience (sabr). What is beautiful patience? We have many kinds of patience. But here, as Allah says so precisely, He says: he endured with beautiful patience.
The scholars say, they say: this beautiful patience is when a person is struck by some calamity (musibah), some misfortune, and he does not lament, does not complain to people, and so on, and so on,

but leaves it to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. When the scholars speak about patience, they divide it into three kinds. The first is "as-sabru 'ala ta'atillah" – they say: patience, or forbearance, in obedience to Allah.
How so? Believe me, dear brothers, it is very hard for a person to be obedient to Allah. We see, for example, someone doing some hard work during the month of Ramadan,

being patient the whole time so as not to drink or eat. Patience in worship (ibadah). It is not easy to come to the dawn prayer (Fajr). Believe me, dear brothers, many people around us fast, but cannot come to the dawn prayer.

That is why patience is needed. Because it is not like that: every morning you have to be precise, punctual, to come to Fajr, to pray Fajr and so on. Or some other act of worship. The second kind, the scholars say: "as-sabru 'anil-ma'siyah".
They say: that a person be patient in abandoning sin. It is very hard for a person to abandon some sin.

It is very hard for a person to lower his gaze; patience is needed there. Especially on warm summer days, when we have what we have in our city, it is very hard for a person to lower his gaze – great patience is needed there.

Or any other sin. The one who used to drink alcohol and wants to quit alcohol, it is very hard for him to quit alcohol – patience is needed there. Or cigarettes, or this, or that, and so on. And the last kind, as the scholars say: patience, or forbearance, in the face of a painful decree, when some trial befalls a person.
Great patience is needed there. And that is what Yaqub did, that is, he was patient in the trial, with beautiful patience, as Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, describes it.

And patience, dear brothers, is at the first blow. Patience is at the first blow. It is narrated that the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him), was passing by a graveyard. There was a woman there who was crying over her child.
Crying and then wailing, and so on, and so on. The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, said to her: "Ittaqillah" – fear Allah, fear Allah, be patient.

And she turned to him and said: "What do you care about my child, about my patience," and so on, and so on. So the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, went away. Someone informed her: "That was the Prophet," and at once she went after him.

When she reached him, she said: "O Messenger of Allah," she said, "I did not know it was you." The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: "As-sabru 'indas-sadmatil-ula" – he says: patience is at the first blow. [unclear] Patience is when a trial first strikes a person, [unclear]

that he says: "Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un." As Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, [unclear]: "Alladhina idha asabathum musibatun qalu inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un" – and when something strikes them, some misfortune, what do they say?

"Truly we belong to Allah and to Allah we shall return." And it is narrated that when Aisha, radiyallahu ta'ala anha (may Allah be pleased with her), was accused of fornication – you all know this, that Aisha, the wife of the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, was accused of fornication –

she spoke with the Prophet, and Abu Bakr, her father, and her mother were there. And the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says – when that fitnah, that trial, had just begun – he says: "If you have done it, repent to Allah and say so, feel free to say so."

She says: "O Messenger of Allah, I did not do it." Then she turned to her mother and said: "Mother, say something." Her mother says: "I don't know what to say, my child," out of respect for the Prophet. "Father, say something." He says: "What can I say, I don't know what to say."

And, it is said, she could not remember the name of Yaqub, alayhis-salam, so she said: "I will say nothing," she said, "except what the father of Yusuf said: fa sabrun jamil – so beautiful patience – wallahul-musta'anu 'ala ma tasifun – and I seek Allah's help against what you describe, against what you are saying."

And she was patient, and after that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, sent down Surah An-Nur, in which He cleared Aisha of those slanders, in which He prescribed punishments for those who accuse chaste Muslim women of fornication, or of [unclear].
And here, in this place, Yaqub was patient, because Yaqub was certain that there was something hidden behind this decree of Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala.

I ask Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, to reward you with every good. I ask Him, the Exalted, that we complete the fast of this Ramadan. I ask Him, the Exalted, to gather us together in Jannah (Paradise) just as He has gathered us in this place, at this prayer. Amin, ya Rabbal-'alamin.
